title: RecruitFlow

basics.tagline: Job Posting, Applicant Tracking & Interview Scheduling

listing.shortDescription: An internal recruitment frontend with separate admin and candidate workspaces — job posting, applicant review, interview scheduling and application tracking in one interface.
listing.fullDescription: Recruiting teams were juggling job postings, applicant emails and interview bookings across different tools, with no shared view of the pipeline. The module gives the recruitment operation two focused workspaces in one app: admins publish structured job listings, review each applicant's full dossier — personal information, resume, cover letter and screening answers — and schedule interviews with a meeting link in a couple of clicks. Candidates browse jobs, apply through a guided multi-step form and track their applications and upcoming interviews from their own dashboard.

cover.imageAlt: Recruitment Module admin dashboard showing hiring analytics

closing.clientOverview: An in-house recruitment operation whose hiring workflow had outgrown its tooling. Postings lived in one place, applications arrived by email with no single home, and booking an interview meant back-and-forth messages and manually pasted meeting links. Nothing could answer the basic question — how many candidates are in screening right now?
closing.conclusion: Recruiters now run the whole cycle from one workspace: publish a job, review a complete applicant dossier, attach a meeting link and move the candidate through the pipeline. Candidates get a guided application flow and a dashboard that shows exactly where they stand — no more chasing status by email.

features.title: Dual workspaces
features.description: Separate admin and candidate interfaces under one codebase, built from the same UI primitives.

features.description: Create, edit and close listings with department, location, employment type and salary bands.

features.title: Applicant pipeline
features.description: Every candidate tracked through New → Interviewing → Hired → Rejected, with a full dossier per applicant.

features.title: Interview scheduling
features.description: Book interviews with meeting-platform selection and a link, recorded against the applicant.

features.title: Structured applications
features.description: Guided multi-step apply flow: personal info, resume upload, screening questions, review and submit.

features.title: Reports & analytics

challenge.summary: Recruitment operations ran on inboxes and spreadsheets — postings lived in one tool, applications in another, and interview booking was email ping-pong.

points.title: Applications scattered
points.description: CVs and cover letters arrived by email with no single place to review a candidate.

points.title: No shared pipeline
points.description: Nobody could see how many candidates sat in screening, interview or offer stages.

points.title: Booking by email
points.description: Scheduling interviews meant back-and-forth messages and manually pasted meeting links.

points.title: Inconsistent submissions
points.description: Free-form applications made it hard to compare candidates against the same questions.

solution.summary: One product, two workspaces. The admin side owns the hiring pipeline end to end; the candidate side makes applying and tracking progress a structured, guided flow.

points.title: One-flow scheduling

Keep every applicant's materials in a single reviewable dossier
Make scheduling an interview a two-click task with a meeting link
Turn applications into a structured flow so candidates can be compared fairly
